sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: A chair is a difficult object.
sentences.zh: 椅子是一种很难设计的物件。

sentences.en: A skyscraper is almost easier.
sentences.zh: 摩天大楼甚至都更容易些。

sentences.en: Those are the words of Mies van der Rohe, one of many architects who have also designed chairs.
sentences.zh: 这是密斯·凡·德·罗的名言，他也是众多设计过椅子的建筑师之一。

sentences.en: Eames, Geary, Adid, Lebeskind, Corbusier, Breuer.
sentences.zh: 伊姆斯、盖里、阿迪德、里伯斯金、柯布西耶、布劳耶。

sentences.en: If they've designed a big building, chances are they've designed a thing on which to sit.
sentences.zh: 如果他们设计过大型建筑，那么他们很可能也设计过供人坐的东西。

sentences.en: And this makes sense that chairs would be signature design pieces for architects.
sentences.zh: 建筑师将椅子作为标志性的设计作品，这在情理之中。

sentences.en: Because chairs are almost like teeny tiny buildings for one person.
sentences.zh: 因为椅子几乎就像是为一个人准备的微型建筑。

sentences.en: Producer Avery Truffleman.
sentences.zh: 制作人艾弗里·特鲁夫曼。

sentences.en: And of course it's not just architects.
sentences.zh: 当然，不仅仅是建筑师。

sentences.en: Designers of all stripes have this love affair with chairs.
sentences.zh: 各行各业的设计师都对椅子有着这种迷恋。

sentences.en: Well I think every designer really would love to design a chair.
sentences.zh: 我觉得每位设计师其实都想设计一把椅子。

sentences.en: I mean there's so many interesting things about chairs.
sentences.zh: 我是说，关于椅子有太多有趣的地方了。

sentences.en: This is designer Bruce Hanna.
sentences.zh: 这位是设计师布鲁斯·汉纳。

sentences.en: I'm a teacher at Pratt Institute in Brooklyn, New York.
sentences.zh: 我在纽约布鲁克林的普瑞特艺术学院任教。

sentences.en: And design things for Knoll for years.
sentences.zh: 并且为诺尔公司设计产品多年。

sentences.en: Including plenty of chairs.
sentences.zh: 包括大量的椅子。

sentences.en: For the office, for the home, everything.
sentences.zh: 办公用的、家用的一切。

sentences.en: Chairs exiSt.
sentences.zh: 椅子是存在的。

sentences.en: They kind of are like placeholders for human beings.
sentences.zh: 它们就像是人类的占位符。

sentences.en: You know, you go into a restaurant that's empty and there's all these little placeholders, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你走进一家空荡荡的餐厅，到处都是这些小小的占位符。

sentences.en: Yet when the people sit in the chair, it disappears.
sentences.zh: 然而当人坐进椅子里，椅子就消失了。

sentences.en: The person replaces the chair.
sentences.zh: 人取代了椅子。

sentences.en: And so there's this distinct challenge for chair designers.
sentences.zh: 所以这对椅子设计师来说是一个独特的挑战。

sentences.en: To make this thing look fantastic when empty.
sentences.zh: 要让这件东西在空置时看起来棒极了。

sentences.en: And remain comfortably invisible when in use.
sentences.zh: 而在使用时又能舒适地隐形。

sentences.en: And Hanna's pursuit of seating innovation actually led to something else.
sentences.zh: 而汉纳对座椅创新的追求实际上带来了别的东西。

sentences.en: When he was experimenting with foam cushioning, Hanna accidentally invented the Nerf ball.
sentences.zh: 当他试验泡沫垫时，汉纳意外发明了耐夫球。

sentences.en: Well actually it's called the foam football.
sentences.zh: 其实它叫泡沫橄榄球。

sentences.en: Still really cool.
sentences.zh: 还是很酷的。

sentences.en: It did come out of designing the chair.
sentences.zh: 它确实源于椅子设计。

sentences.en: I mean we're much more interested in the chair.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们对椅子更感兴趣。

sentences.en: Yes, those designers sure do love chairs.
sentences.zh: 是的，那些设计师确实很爱椅子。

sentences.en: Love them.
sentences.zh: 非常爱。

sentences.en: They keep turning out new ones all the time.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在不断推出新款。

sentences.en: Which brings me to one of my favorite headlines from The Onion.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起了《洋葱报》我最喜欢的标题之一。

sentences.en: Quote,
sentences.zh: 引用如下：

sentences.en: Report confirms no need to make new chairs for the time being.
sentences.zh: 报道证实目前无需制造新椅子。

sentences.en: Because yeah, there are already a lot.
sentences.zh: 因为没错，已经有很多了。

sentences.en: I think you could say that about anything.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以对任何事物都这么说。

sentences.en: When we have enough cars, let's stop making cars.
sentences.zh: 当我们有足够的汽车时，就停止制造汽车吧。

sentences.en: Personally, I wouldn't be against that.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我不反对这一点。

sentences.en: But new chairs are always coming out, Hanna says, to fit our ever-changing needs.
sentences.zh: 但汉纳说，新椅子总是在不断推出，以适应我们不断变化的需求。

sentences.en: Because chairs determine how we use a space.
sentences.zh: 因为椅子决定了我们如何使用空间。

sentences.en: Hanna brought up this great example of seating in cafes.
sentences.zh: 汉纳提到了咖啡馆座椅这个很好的例子。

sentences.en: Cafes used to be places for talking.
sentences.zh: 咖啡馆过去是谈话的地方。

sentences.en: And now they're places for working.
sentences.zh: 而现在它们是工作的地方。

sentences.en: So people are sitting and interacting differently.
sentences.zh: 所以人们坐着和互动的方式不同了。

sentences.en: And so the furniture evolves along with the space and the activities.
sentences.zh: 因此家具也随着空间和活动而演变。

sentences.en: Throughout our lives, we have been told to sit down.
sentences.zh: 在我们的一生中，我们一直被告知要坐下。

sentences.en: In school, in the office, in the polite company of a dinner party, in a car or a plane or a bus or a movie theater.
sentences.zh: 在学校、办公室、正式晚宴上、车里、飞机上、公交车上或电影院里。

sentences.en: Sitting is the default.
sentences.zh: 坐着是默认状态。

sentences.en: We spend a lot of time in chairs.
sentences.zh: 我们花了很多时间坐在椅子上。

sentences.en: But I'm sure you heard all the talk lately about how unhealthy chairs are.
sentences.zh: 但我相信你最近一定听过关于椅子有多不健康的讨论。

sentences.en: Especially if you listen to public radio, which I bet you do, you beautiful nerd.
sentences.zh: 特别是如果你听公共广播的话，我敢打赌你听过，你这个可爱的书呆子。

sentences.en: First we'll talk about chronic sitting.
sentences.zh: 首先我们来谈谈长期久坐。

sentences.en: Are you sitting down?
sentences.zh: 你现在坐着吗？

sentences.en: Well, you might want to stand up.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可能想站起来。

sentences.en: It turns out that sitting down can be bad for your health.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，久坐可能对你的健康有害。

sentences.en: And those who were sitting more were substantially more likely to die.
sentences.zh: 而那些坐得更多的人死亡的可能性要大得多。

sentences.en: Jeez.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: I think I found like five articles with the headline,
sentences.zh: 我想我找到了大约五篇标题为以下内容的文章：

sentences.en: Sitting is the New Smoking.
sentences.zh: 久坐是新的吸烟方式。

sentences.en: The absolute number of hours that you sit is directly correlated with mortality from all causes.
sentences.zh: 你坐着的绝对小时数与各种原因导致的死亡率直接相关。

sentences.en: Cancer, heart attack, and stroke.
sentences.zh: 癌症、心脏病和中风。

sentences.en: And it doesn't matter how many hours you spend in the gym as compensation.
sentences.zh: 而且你在健身房花多少小时来补偿都无济于事。

sentences.en: This is Professor Galen Krantz.
sentences.zh: 这位是盖伦·克兰茨教授。

sentences.en: You come in and the secretary says, have a seat.
sentences.zh: 你走进来，秘书说，请坐。

sentences.en: She doesn't know.
sentences.zh: 她不知道。

sentences.en: She's wishing you death.
sentences.zh: 她在祝你早死。

sentences.en: You know, it's a death wish.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一种死亡诅咒。

sentences.en: This research, along with those scary headlines, has led to a new market for medicine ball chairs,
sentences.zh: 这项研究，连同那些可怕的标题，催生了一个新的市场，包括健身球椅、

sentences.en: adjustable chairs, standing desks, treadmill desks.
sentences.zh: 可调节椅子、站立式办公桌、跑步机办公桌。

sentences.en: The chair backlash is upon us.
sentences.zh: 反椅子浪潮已经来临。

sentences.en: And Berkeley architecture professor Galen Krantz totally nailed it, way before anyone else.
sentences.zh: 而伯克利大学建筑学教授盖伦·克兰茨早在其他人之前就完全看透了这一点。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: It is nice that people are saying that I was prescient, and I wasn't prescient.
sentences.zh: 人们说我有先见之明固然很好，但我并没有什么先见之明。

sentences.en: Everybody else was just blind.
sentences.zh: 其他人只是视而不见罢了。

sentences.en: In 1998, Krantz published a book called The Chair, Rethinking Culture, Body, and Design.
sentences.zh: 1998年，克兰茨出版了一本书，名为《椅子：重新思考文化、身体与设计》。

sentences.en: And the argument of the chair is that we should stop sitting in chairs.
sentences.zh: 而这本书的论点是，我们应该停止坐在椅子上。

sentences.en: At least we should stop sitting in them for so long.
sentences.zh: 至少我们应该停止坐那么久。

sentences.en: Up to three hours doesn't seem to have much consequence.
sentences.zh: 坐三个小时以内似乎没什么大碍。

sentences.en: But Professor Krantz takes innovative chair sitting to another level.
sentences.zh: 但克兰茨教授将创新的坐姿提升到了另一个层面。

sentences.en: I try to eliminate all conventional chairs in my own life.
sentences.zh: 我试图在自己的生活中消除所有传统的椅子。

sentences.en: Which presented a challenge when I went to go interview her.
sentences.zh: 这在我去采访她时带来了一个挑战。

sentences.en: I wonder, let's see, how shall we sit?
sentences.zh: 我在想，看看，我们该怎么坐呢？

sentences.en: Professor Krantz's house was full of floor cushions, tatami mats, and lots and lots of
sentences.zh: 克兰茨教授的家里到处都是地板垫、榻榻米，还有许许多多

sentences.en: unconventional hybrid chairs.
sentences.zh: 非传统的混合椅。

sentences.en: Like a medicine ball on an office chair chassis.
sentences.zh: 比如安装在办公椅底座上的健身球。

sentences.en: And one that looked like a sleek, pared-down horse saddle.
sentences.zh: 还有一个看起来像光滑、极简的马鞍。

sentences.en: And when she's not in her home seating oasis and out in public,
sentences.zh: 当她不在家里的座椅绿洲，而在公共场合时，

sentences.en: Professor Krantz does a lot of standing.
sentences.zh: 克兰茨教授经常站着。

sentences.en: And instead of sitting when she gets tired, she opts to kneel, or squat, or lie down.
sentences.zh: 当她累了的时候，她选择跪着、蹲着或躺下，而不是坐着。

sentences.en: I laid down in a bank and somebody came up and asked me if I was having a heart attack.
sentences.zh: 我曾在银行里躺下，有人走过来问我是不是心脏病发作了。

sentences.en: Which was kind of them.
sentences.zh: 他们倒是挺好心的。

sentences.en: You know, I understand.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我理解。

sentences.en: But I said, no, I'm fine.
sentences.zh: 但我说，不，我很好。

sentences.en: I'm just resting because the line is so long.
sentences.zh: 我只是在休息，因为排队太长了。

sentences.en: You've got to be gutsy to actually avoid the chairs everywhere.
sentences.zh: 你得有胆量才能真正避开随处可见的椅子。

sentences.en: So how did the rest of us get suckered into the seated position?
sentences.zh: 那么我们其他人是怎么被诱导进入坐姿的呢？

sentences.en: Well, it all started when we got off the farm.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这一切始于我们离开农场的时候。

sentences.en: In the 20th century, we moved from being an agricultural economy, where most people worked
sentences.zh: 在20世纪，我们从农业经济转型，那时大多数人都在

sentences.en: on farMs.
sentences.zh: 农场工作。

sentences.en: And then we moved into a manufacturing economy, where a lot of people worked in factories.
sentences.zh: 然后我们进入了制造业经济，许多人在工厂工作。

sentences.en: And some sat, some stood to work the machines along the conveyor belts.
sentences.zh: 有些人坐着，有些人站着操作传送带旁的机器。

sentences.en: Not to over-romanticize life on the farm.
sentences.zh: 并不是要过度美化农场生活。

sentences.en: They were still doing back-breaking work.
sentences.zh: 他们依然在从事繁重的体力劳动。

sentences.en: They just probably had better posture and less carpal tunnel syndrome.
sentences.zh: 他们只是可能有更好的姿势，更少的腕管综合症。

sentences.en: And then we moved into a service economy.
sentences.zh: 然后我们进入了服务业经济。

sentences.en: And that seems to be where the chair really took off and became the dominant apparatus
sentences.zh: 而那似乎是椅子真正兴起并成为我们生活中主导工具的时候。

sentences.en: for our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们的生活。

sentences.en: And then when we settled into the service economy, sitting became the way to type and file and
sentences.zh: 当我们进入服务业经济时，坐着成了打字、归档和

sentences.en: fill out paperwork.
sentences.zh: 填写文书工作的方式。

sentences.en: You could do that standing, but for reasons I don't fully understand, we did it sitting.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以站着做这些，但出于我不完全理解的原因，我们选择了坐着。

sentences.en: And so office chairs become the chairs, the chairs that people spend most of their day
sentences.zh: 于是办公椅成了椅子，成了人们一天中大部分时间所处的

sentences.en: in.
sentences.zh: 椅子。

sentences.en: And until very recent history, they were not made to fit your body.
sentences.zh: 直到最近，它们都不是为了适应你的身体而制造的。

sentences.en: They were made to fit your job.
sentences.zh: 它们是为了适应你的工作而制造的。

sentences.en: So you had a managerial one.
sentences.zh: 所以你有管理人员用的椅子。

sentences.en: You had a middle managerial one.
sentences.zh: 你有中层管理人员用的椅子。

sentences.en: You had a secretarial one.
sentences.zh: 你有秘书用的椅子。

sentences.en: You had a task chair.
sentences.zh: 你有工作椅。

sentences.en: Bruce Hanna had to design a few of these kinds of office chairs.
sentences.zh: 布鲁斯·汉纳不得不设计几种这样的办公椅。

sentences.en: The status-oriented chair design meant that in some cases...
sentences.zh: 这种以地位为导向的椅子设计意味着在某些情况下……

sentences.en: You had the 120-pound executive sitting in a gigantic chair, because it really was about
sentences.zh: 你会有120磅重的行政人员坐在巨大的椅子上，因为这确实关乎

sentences.en: his presence when he wasn't there, or her presence when he wasn't there.
sentences.zh: 他不在时他的存在感，或者她不在时她的存在感。

sentences.en: And then you had the 160-pound assistant secretary sitting in this tiny little chair.
sentences.zh: 然后你会有160磅重的助理秘书坐在这种极小的椅子上。

sentences.en: For the most part, status trumped ergonomics.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，地位高于人体工程学。

sentences.en: And then along comes 1992, the Aeron chair, where it's the same chair, it just comes in
sentences.zh: 然后到了1992年，Aeron椅出现了，它还是同一把椅子，只是有

sentences.en: three sizes.
sentences.zh: 三种尺寸。

sentences.en: It's a T-shirt.
sentences.zh: 它就像一件T恤。

sentences.en: A small one, a medium one, and a big one.
sentences.zh: 小号、中号和大号。

sentences.en: But everybody gets all of the adjustments.
sentences.zh: 但每个人都能获得所有的调节功能。

sentences.en: They get arMs.
sentences.zh: 他们有扶手。

sentences.en: They get everything they need to work, because everyone is working equally hard in the office.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有工作所需的一切，因为办公室里的每个人都在同样努力地工作。

sentences.en: The Herman Miller Aeron chair.
sentences.zh: 赫尔曼·米勒的Aeron椅。

sentences.en: You've seen an Aeron chair.
sentences.zh: 你一定见过Aeron椅。

sentences.en: It's got this mesh-looking back.
sentences.zh: 它有这种网状的靠背。

sentences.en: And you've probably heard it mentioned on public radio, you beautiful nerd.
sentences.zh: 你可能在公共广播里听到过它的名字，你这个可爱的书呆子。

sentences.en: Support for NPR comes from Sit for Life and Herman Miller, featuring the Aeron chair, including
sentences.zh: NPR的支持来自Sit for Life和赫尔曼·米勒，主打Aeron椅，包括

sentences.en: the true black color.
sentences.zh: 纯黑色款。

sentences.en: They're usually black, or true black.
sentences.zh: 它们通常是黑色的，或者是纯黑色的。

sentences.en: There's one of them everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都有它们的身影。

sentences.en: I was surprised when I walked into the studio today.
sentences.zh: 今天走进录音室时我很惊讶。

sentences.en: You don't have a couple here, you know, because they're everywhere.
sentences.zh: 你们这里居然没有几把，你知道的，因为它们无处不在。

sentences.en: They're ubiquitous.
sentences.zh: 它们无处不在。

sentences.en: They're the ubiquitous chair.
sentences.zh: 它们是无处不在的椅子。

sentences.en: And the Aeron chair brought on this age of ergonomic office chairs that look like little
sentences.zh: Aeron椅开启了人体工程学办公椅的时代，它们看起来就像小

sentences.en: robots.
sentences.zh: 机器人。

sentences.en: They display their technology as a selling point.
sentences.zh: 他们把技术作为卖点来展示。

sentences.en: And they show off their swivels and their adjustments and their ergonomic technology.
sentences.zh: 他们炫耀着椅子上的旋转装置、调节功能以及人体工学技术。

sentences.en: The Aeron chair defined what an office chair ought to look like.
sentences.zh: Aeron办公椅定义了办公椅应有的模样。

sentences.en: Right now, I think it's what society says, that that will make me comfortable.
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为这就是社会所说的，认为那会让我感到舒适。

sentences.en: That piece of machinery.
sentences.zh: 那台机器。

sentences.en: And no one guessed that these expensive pieces of machinery would sell like hotcakes.
sentences.zh: 没人想到这些昂贵的机器会如此畅销。

sentences.en: No one except Galen Grants.
sentences.zh: 除了盖伦·克兰茨（Galen Krantz）之外，没人想到。

sentences.en: When my book first came out, people said, well, you know, nobody's going to pay for an ordinary
sentences.zh: 我的书刚出版时，人们说，嗯，你知道，没人会花钱给一个普通职员

sentences.en: clerk to have an adjustable chair with all the bells and whistles.
sentences.zh: 买一把功能齐全、可以调节的椅子。

sentences.en: Oh, that's way too expensive.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太贵了。

sentences.en: That'll never happen.
sentences.zh: 那永远不会发生。

sentences.en: Well, then there was repetitive strain injury and a whole lot of lawsuits.
sentences.zh: 好吧，后来出现了重复性劳损，还有一大堆诉讼。

sentences.en: And insurance companies suddenly thought it was a lot cheaper to buy those fancy adjustable
sentences.zh: 保险公司突然觉得，购买那些花哨的可调节椅子

sentences.en: chairs than to pay for medical bills.
sentences.zh: 比支付医疗费要便宜得多。

sentences.en: Krantz is a fan of what she calls body conscious design and considers any chair that takes the
sentences.zh: 克兰茨是她所称的“身体意识设计”的拥护者，她认为任何考虑到

sentences.en: human figure into account is a vast improvement over, say, a beanbag chair.
sentences.zh: 人体形态的椅子，都比懒人沙发之类的东西有了巨大的改进。

sentences.en: But Krantz argues that some of those bells and whistles on office chairs actually don't
sentences.zh: 但克兰茨认为，办公椅上的一些花哨功能实际上并没有

sentences.en: help that much.
sentences.zh: 多大帮助。

sentences.en: Specifically, those ergonomic chair backs.
sentences.zh: 特别是那些人体工学椅背。

sentences.en: Because in all likelihood, you are probably sitting in this chair while working at a desk.
sentences.zh: 因为很有可能，你坐在椅子上时是在办公桌前工作。

sentences.en: And the desk, it turns out, is the chair's devious accomplice.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，办公桌是椅子的邪恶帮凶。

sentences.en: The true villain is the table.
sentences.zh: 真正的罪魁祸首是桌子。

sentences.en: Flat surfaces force you to lean over, so you never really take advantage of the chair back.
sentences.zh: 平坦的桌面迫使你俯身，所以你从未真正利用过椅背。

sentences.en: The chair in particular asks us to sit at this right angle position, but most of our work
sentences.zh: 椅子特别要求我们以这种直角姿势坐着，但我们大部分的工作

sentences.en: is forward oriented.
sentences.zh: 都是面向前方的。

sentences.en: Clerical work, reading, writing checks, and eating even, or drinking tea and coffee, and
sentences.zh: 文书工作、阅读、写支票，甚至吃饭、喝茶喝咖啡，

sentences.en: all the, everything's forward.
sentences.zh: 所有的一切，都是朝前的。

sentences.en: So you bend forward, or more likely slump.
sentences.zh: 所以你会向前弯腰，或者更可能的是瘫坐着。

sentences.en: Even if you have excellent posture, it's hard to avoid leaning over your keyboard, or your
sentences.zh: 即使你的坐姿非常端正，也很难避免俯身去够键盘、

sentences.en: dinner, or your book.
sentences.zh: 晚餐或书本。

sentences.en: So the head gets seduced into coming forward, and then the spine turns into a big C shape.
sentences.zh: 于是头部被诱导向前，脊椎就变成了一个大大的“C”形。

sentences.en: And Galen Krantz says that when you curve your spine into the C shape, it's bad for the
sentences.zh: 盖伦·克兰茨说，当你把脊椎弯成“C”形时，这当然对脊椎不好，

sentences.en: spine, of course, but it also compresses your organs, which is really bad.
sentences.zh: 而且还会压迫你的内脏，这真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: Especially for hours on end, throughout the day, in an office chair.
sentences.zh: 特别是在办公椅上一坐就是好几个小时，整天如此。

sentences.en: And because of this horrible chair-desk dynamic, chair designers can't solve much by adding
sentences.zh: 正因为这种糟糕的“椅-桌”互动，椅子设计师通过在椅背上增加

sentences.en: ergonomic elements to the chair backs.
sentences.zh: 人体工学元素并不能解决太多问题。

sentences.en: Actually, Professor Krantz thinks we should do away with back support entirely.
sentences.zh: 事实上，克兰茨教授认为我们应该完全取消背部支撑。

sentences.en: I think back support is a big mistake, and it's weakened our backs.
sentences.zh: 我认为背部支撑是一个巨大的错误，它削弱了我们的背部。

sentences.en: If you support something, you usually weaken it.
sentences.zh: 如果你支撑某样东西，通常就会削弱它。

sentences.en: So if you're in a situation where you must, must, sit in a chair, Krantz says it's best
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你处于必须坐着的情况，克兰茨说最好

sentences.en: to ignore the chair back, and sit yourself right at the edge of your seat.
sentences.zh: 忽略椅背，坐在座位的最边缘。

sentences.en: Right out to the edge.
sentences.zh: 一直坐到边缘。

sentences.en: That way you don't get seduced to using the chair back.
sentences.zh: 这样你就不会被诱导去使用椅背了。

sentences.en: You have your own torso strength to keep you upright.
sentences.zh: 你要靠自己躯干的力量来保持直立。

sentences.en: With this strategy of getting your sit bones out to the edge of the chair, you're turning
sentences.zh: 通过这种让坐骨移到椅子边缘的策略，你实际上是把它

sentences.en: it into a stool.
sentences.zh: 变成了一张凳子。

sentences.en: Stools, Krantz says, are a good alternative to chairs, because they don't have back support,
sentences.zh: 克兰茨说，凳子是椅子的良好替代品，因为它们没有背部支撑，

sentences.en: and they get your body out of the C shape.
sentences.zh: 而且能让你的身体摆脱“C”形。

sentences.en: It positions the body halfway between sitting and standing.
sentences.zh: 它将身体定位在坐姿和站姿之间。

sentences.en: And if you take that body position and lean it backwards...
sentences.zh: 如果你保持那种身体姿势并向后倾斜……

sentences.en: What do you get?
sentences.zh: 你会得到什么？

sentences.en: A lounge chair.
sentences.zh: 一把躺椅。

sentences.en: And that's how I'm positioned right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在就是这种姿势。

sentences.en: Yeah, Galen Krantz was reclining in a lounge chair for this interview.
sentences.zh: 没错，盖伦·克兰茨在这次采访中正斜靠在躺椅上。

sentences.en: I'll be in the lounge, and I'll have you in the rocking chair facing me.
sentences.zh: “我会坐在躺椅上，让你坐在面对我的摇椅上。”

sentences.en: And she put me in a rocking chair, because unlike a normal chair, it allows for more fluidity
sentences.zh: 她让我坐在摇椅上，因为与普通椅子不同，它允许更多的流动性

sentences.en: and movement.
sentences.zh: 和运动。

sentences.en: And this all sounds great and healthy and fun.
sentences.zh: 这一切听起来都很棒、很健康、很有趣。

sentences.en: But in practice, I was sitting all the way forward, rocking right to the very front,
sentences.zh: 但在实践中，我一直坐在最前面，摇到最前端，

sentences.en: stretching my microphone out to Krantz, who was lying back in her lounge chair.
sentences.zh: 把麦克风伸向躺在躺椅上的克兰茨。

sentences.en: And it hurt.
sentences.zh: 这很痛苦。

sentences.en: I just wanted two chairs and a flat desk to rest my arm on.
sentences.zh: 我只想要两把椅子和一张平坦的桌子来支撑我的手臂。

sentences.en: But I don't know, maybe I just wasn't used to this alternative world yet.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道，也许我只是还不习惯这个另类的世界。

sentences.en: Maybe I needed to get acclimated, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 也许我需要适应一下，我不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, Professor Krantz looked pretty comfortable in her lounge chair.
sentences.zh: 我是说，克兰茨教授在她的躺椅上看起来相当舒服。

sentences.en: Before people got so into standing desks and treadmill desks, Professor Krantz was sure that
sentences.zh: 在人们热衷于站立式办公桌和跑步机办公桌之前，克兰茨教授就确信

sentences.en: lounge chairs and lounge chair desks would replace chair sitting.
sentences.zh: 躺椅和躺椅式办公桌会取代传统的坐姿。

sentences.en: Of all the solutions to the seating problem, the lounge chair is the solution that requires
sentences.zh: 在所有解决久坐问题的方法中，躺椅是需要

sentences.en: the least physical effort, while still supporting the human body in a healthy way.
sentences.zh: 体力消耗最少，同时又能以健康方式支撑人体的方法。

sentences.en: But it's not like there's one single piece of furniture that will correct all the problems
sentences.zh: 但这并不是说有一件单一的家具就能解决所有

sentences.en: of chair sitting.
sentences.zh: 久坐带来的问题。

sentences.en: No, lounge chair is not the answer.
sentences.zh: 不，躺椅不是答案。

sentences.en: There's no the answer.
sentences.zh: 没有所谓的“答案”。

sentences.en: What we need is variety.
sentences.zh: 我们需要的是多样性。

sentences.en: The best posture is the next posture.
sentences.zh: 最好的姿势是下一个姿势。

sentences.en: Bruce Hanna agrees.
sentences.zh: 布鲁斯·汉纳（Bruce Hanna）表示赞同。

sentences.en: The more variation in your day, the better off.
sentences.zh: 你一天中的变化越多，情况就越好。

sentences.en: But he's not chair avoidant.
sentences.zh: 但他并不排斥椅子。

sentences.en: Sitting is the new smoking?
sentences.zh: “久坐是新的吸烟方式”？

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: We should be up and running every day.
sentences.zh: 我们应该每天起来跑动。

sentences.en: Run, run, run, run, run, run, run, run.
sentences.zh: 跑，跑，跑，跑，跑，跑，跑，跑。

sentences.en: Does that mean that all restaurants will be running in place at restaurants?
sentences.zh: 那是不是意味着所有的餐馆里的人都要在原地跑步？

sentences.en: There'll be treadmills, right?
sentences.zh: 会有跑步机，对吧？

sentences.en: Will nothing be sacred?
sentences.zh: 难道没有什么东西是神圣不可侵犯的吗？

sentences.en: I like to sit.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢坐着。

sentences.en: I want to sit down.
sentences.zh: 我想坐下来。

sentences.en: An ideal space to live or to work could be full of unconventional mismatched chairs for
sentences.zh: 一个理想的生活或工作空间，应该摆满各种非传统的、不配套的椅子，

sentences.en: you to try out and cycle through, like in Galen Krantz's dining room.
sentences.zh: 供你尝试和轮换使用，就像盖伦·克兰茨的餐厅里那样。

sentences.en: People say, oh, wow, you have a lot of chairs.
sentences.zh: 人们说，哦，哇，你有这么多椅子。

sentences.en: I say, oh, yeah, it's a chair museum.
sentences.zh: 我说，哦，是的，这是一个椅子博物馆。

sentences.en: And I say, oh, be sure to try them all.
sentences.zh: 我说，哦，一定要都试一试。

sentences.en: And people do.
sentences.zh: 人们确实会试。

sentences.en: They like, they say, well, I've sat in that one.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，嗯，我坐过那把了。

sentences.en: Can I go try that one halfway through the dinner?
sentences.zh: 晚餐吃到一半，我可以去试试那把吗？

sentences.en: You know, the middle class thing is you want everything to match.
sentences.zh: 你知道，中产阶级的想法是你希望一切都配套。

sentences.en: And it's fun that these don't match.
sentences.zh: 而这些椅子不配套反而很有趣。

sentences.en: Everybody loves it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都喜欢这样。

sentences.en: Trying out all the different attitudes towards seating reform.
sentences.zh: 尝试所有关于座椅改革的不同态度。

sentences.en: But the solution isn't just a, like, only in Berkeley kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 但这个解决方案不仅仅是那种“仅限伯克利”的事情。

sentences.en: So maybe in this one case, this one exception, the onion is wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以也许在这个案例中，这个唯一的例外，洋葱新闻（The Onion）是错的。

sentences.en: We don't need fewer things to sit on.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要更少的坐具。

sentences.en: It turns out we need more.
sentences.zh: 事实证明我们需要更多。

sentences.en: And all different kinds.
sentences.zh: 而且是各种各样的。

sentences.en: Stools, perches, lounge chairs.
sentences.zh: 凳子、高脚凳、躺椅。

sentences.en: And hell, throw in some desk redesigns while you're at it.
sentences.zh: 见鬼，顺便再重新设计一下办公桌吧。

sentences.en: Ones that rise up to meet us like drafting tables.
sentences.zh: 那种像绘图桌一样升起来迎合我们的桌子。

sentences.en: Design more.
sentences.zh: 多设计一些。

sentences.en: Much, much more.
sentences.zh: 多得多。

sentences.en: Bring me more chairs.
sentences.zh: 给我更多的椅子。

sentences.en: Yes, all the chairs.
sentences.zh: 是的，所有的椅子。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99% Invisible》由……制作。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 local public radio, KALW in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 本地公共广播电台 KALW 的一个项目。

sentences.en: And produced out of the offices of ArcSign in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 在加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心美丽的 ArcSign 办公室制作。

sentences.en: You can find this show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Facebook 上找到并关注这个节目。

sentences.en: All of us are on Twitter, Instagram, and Spotify.
sentences.zh: 我们都在 Twitter、Instagram 和 Spotify 上。

sentences.en: But to find out more about this story, including cool pictures and links,
sentences.zh: 但要了解更多关于这个故事的信息，包括精美的图片和链接，

sentences.en: and listen to all the episodes of 99% Invisible, you must go to 99PI.
sentences.zh: 并收听《99% Invisible》的所有剧集，你必须访问 99PI。

sentences.en: Dot org.
sentences.zh: 点org。
